title: Feasibility study of a VR-based exercise therapy for patients receiving specialized palliative care
summary:
Patients receiving specialized palliative care (SPC) often experience a high symptom burden, including fatigue, pain, and reduced physical capacity. Although physical activity can help maintain or improve physical functioning and quality of life, participation in exercise-based interventions in the palliative care setting is often limited by disease-related and structural barriers.

In our study, we aim to address these barriers by implementing a VR-based exercise intervention in a palliative care setting. Using a virtual reality headset (Meta Quest 3), patients can choose between two individually adaptable applications: a meditative exercise (FunFitLand: Flowfit) and a climbing application (ClimbXR). By combining physical activity with immersion in a virtual environment, the intervention is intended to provide a motivating form of therapy that promotes physical activity while also offering distraction from disease-related symptoms and discomfort.

The primary aim of this study is to assess the feasibility of the VR-based exercise intervention and to determine whether it is well tolerated and accepted by patients. In addition, the study will explore potential effects on fatigue and quality of life.
conditions: Patients receiving specialized palliative care with a high burden of disease- and symptom-related distress, particularly fatigue, pain, reduced physical capacity, impaired mobility, dyspnea, anxiety and depressive symptoms, and reduced quality of life. The study includes patients with a range of advanced, life-limiting conditions.

interventions.name: VR-based exercise therapy (maximum of 2 sessions per week during the inpatient stay; maximum of 15 minutes per session, followed by a 5-minute structured debriefing interview)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Underlying incurable disease
- Receiving specialized palliative care
- No medical contraindication to study participation
- Physician-confirmed eligibility to participate
- Written informed consent
- Sufficient German language skills
Exclusion criteria:
- Neurological, muscular, or musculoskeletal conditions that preclude the safe performance of the exercises, including clinically relevant cervical spine disorders
- Uncontrolled dizziness
- Severe cardiopulmonary disease (ejection fraction <30%)
- Newly diagnosed or progressive, uncontrolled central nervous system (CNS) metastases
- Expected life expectancy of <3 months
- Bone metastases with an acute risk of pathological fracture
- ECOG Performance Status of 4
- Acute pulmonary embolism
- Acute myocardial infarction
- Aortic aneurysm requiring surgical intervention
- Tension pneumothorax
- Insufficient German language skills
- Active infection

Additional VR-specific exclusion criteria:

- Photosensitive epilepsy
- Severe claustrophobia
- Severe uncorrected visual or hearing impairment preventing use of the HMD
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Acute vertigo or known vestibular disorder
